A0249.title: After-Sales Review
A0249.definition: Review orders, logistics, discounts, and user behavior during refund, return, compensation, gift recovery, and entitlement revocation to block abnormal after-sales arbitrage.
A0249.description:
After-sales review checks order amount, discount details, payment state, logistics trace, delivery evidence, historical after-sales rate, account linkage, and product flow when users request refunds, returns, refusals, compensation, gift retention, discount rollback, or entitlement revocation. High-risk orders can be routed to manual review, delayed refunds, return-before-refund, gift recovery, coupon revocation, or abnormal-account freezing.

This control handles downstream losses from fast-refund arbitrage, malicious returns, after-sales entitlement abuse, and discount stacking arbitrage. Its focus is not to block all refunds, but to identify abnormal patterns such as claiming benefits before refunding, keeping rewards after refunds, fake returns, and centralized recycling/resale, then feed the handling result back to upstream risk control.
A0249.limitation: After-sales review is constrained by insufficient evidence, delayed logistics data, platform service commitments, and user experience. Attackers may evade review through dispersed accounts, real logistics, proxy ordering, or normal-user assistance. Overly strict review can harm legitimate after-sales users, while loose review can be exploited at scale, so risk scoring and manual review must be layered.
